# Virelo

> Virelo turns local video folders into a private streaming-style library. Files remain on the user's device.

## Main pages

- [Virelo home](https://virelo.riyo.me/): Product overview, privacy model, and ways to use Virelo.
- [Setup guide](https://virelo.riyo.me/setup): CLI setup for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android with Termux.
- [Web player](https://virelo.riyo.me/app): Browser-only player for user-selected local folders.

## Project links

- [Web source](https://github.com/VireloHQ/Virelo-Web): Browser player source code and issue tracker.
- [CLI source](https://github.com/VireloHQ/Virelo): Local server source code, releases, and issue tracker.
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/virelo): Install and run Virelo with npx.

## Key facts

- The web player does not require an account and does not upload selected video files.
- Virelo CLI 0.4+ requires sign-in. Create the first administrator on the server device using localhost.
- The web player runs client-side in the browser.
- The CLI can serve a local video folder with `npx virelo`.
- The web player needs no installation; supported browsers can optionally install it as a PWA.
- Virelo includes Explorer navigation, named playlists, editable queues, optional volume leveling and a swipeable Shorts feed for portrait videos.
- Four controller styles, custom accent colors and five interface languages are available.
- Automatic movie/series information and artwork, accounts, library permissions and administrator announcements require the self-hosted server, not the browser-only player.
